neighbours.label: carbon dioxide / CO2 (and carbon) as an atmospheric or chemical substance
fire: Burning coal releases large amounts of CO2 into the atmosphere each year.

Scientists measured rising CO2 levels at the observatory in Hawaii.
When forests burn, stored carbon returns to the atmosphere as gas.
The factory captures CO2 from its chimneys and stores it underground.
Oceans have taken up roughly a quarter of human carbon dioxide emissions.
Fermentation produces ethanol and CO2 as the yeast consumes sugar.
Ice cores show that atmospheric carbon dioxide was lower before 1800.

When forests burn, stored heat returns to the atmosphere as smoke.
The factory filters dust from its chimneys and stores it in bins.
